title: Great soloists are not always good clinicians
summary: He only uses players who can also teach; instrument companies overlook that great soloists often can't explain what they do.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I think once you told me, maybe within the last year, that there are some people who may be dynamite players, but they don't assume that role of helping others too well, so you don't give a --
No, we don't use them, no.
You just use the people who --
People who can get their job done, that's right. And not every soloist has to be a good clinician.

And I think this is something where the instrument companies and people who set up these things are losing sight. They know if a guy's a great soloist. And he comes in and says, 'Well, how did you do that, sir?' 'Man, I don't know.'
Yeah, just do it. Get up here and blow, man.
